question.problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}\frac{2}{\sqrt{13}} & \frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} \\ -\frac{3}{\sqrt{13}} & \frac{2}{\sqrt{13}}\end{aligned}],\,Q=[\begin{aligned}8 & 2\sqrt{3} \\ -4\sqrt{3} & -3\end{aligned}]
$$

Find $|\text{det}(PQ)|$ given that $P$ is an orthogonal matrix.
question.worked_solution:
We use the following facts: 

- The determinant of a product is equal to the product of the determinants.

- The determinant of an orthogonal matrix $P$ is equal to $\pm 1.$

Applying these ideas, we get the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\text{det}(PQ)| & =|\text{det}(P)\cdot \text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|(\pm 1)\cdot \text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|\pm 1|\cdot |\text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|\text{det}(Q)| \\  & =|8\cdot (-3)-2\sqrt{3}\cdot (-4\sqrt{3})| \\  & =0\end{aligned}
$$
